More importantly, the core issue is the logic used to find the "fifth section." The agent jumped to a conclusion without verifying the actual list of sections on the Cornell Law website. Furthermore, the "Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure" generally do not contain a significant number of rules titled with "witnesses" compared to the "Federal Rules of Evidence" (which contains numerous rules regarding witnesses). If the agent proceeds down the wrong path (Bankruptcy), it will fail to find the article with the most "witnesses" titles (likely Evidence), leading to an incorrect answer. The agent needs to first list or view the sections to confirm the alphabetical order before selecting the fifth one.
